title: Battle protocol hole frontiers order weapon-attack, save-gated-spell, spell-attack, Hit Point restoration, Command, and Stat Block action procedure fills before resolution
reason: Weapon-attack scope: the SRD attack structure fixes Choose a Target before resolving the attack, and Resolve the Attack makes the Attack Roll before hit damage dice. Save-gated-spell scope: the SRD defines affected targets or an area as the source of saving throws, the save result is determined by that effect, and damaging save effects roll damage after the affected creatures' save outcomes are known. Spell-attack scope: the same SRD attack structure applies to attacks made as part of a spell, the spellcasting rules define Spell Attack Rolls, and spell damage dice are rolled only after a hit unless a spell says otherwise. Typed spell-attack damage-type choice is modeled as a runtime Spell Invocation frontier that can be supplied alongside target choice before the Spell Attack Roll. Hit Point restoration scope: spell healing chooses a target or target list before the spell healing roll supplies the restored Hit Point amount; feature healing-pool procedures expose one distribution frontier whose allocations are chosen before the feature resolves allocation legality, resource spend, restored Hit Points, and the shared Hit Point lifecycle owner applies any zero-Hit-Point cleanup. Command scope: the SRD says the caster chooses a command option, the target makes a Wisdom Saving Throw, and failed-save targets follow that option on their next turn. The reducer exposes target list and Command option as initial sibling holes but its resolution protocol requests target list before option choice before Saving Throw outcome; this is a reducer protocol choice not prescribed by the SRD. Failed Saving Throw outcomes must resolve before pending next-turn Command effects exist. On the target turn, Grovel applies Prone and ends the turn, Drop releases held objects after table-owned held-object facts are supplied when no canonical loadout exists, Halt suppresses Movement, Action, and Bonus Action through turn resources, and Approach/Flee admit Movement fills only after their pending command act opens. Approach/Flee route facts and Flee fastest-available validation remain caller/table facts carried by the Movement fill; opportunity-attack continuation is an interrupt frontier, not a Command ordering hole. The QNT owners record these frontier stages over the B01/B02 hole/fill vocabulary. For save-gated condition spells with a target-list and condition-choice hole, and for typed spell attacks with damage-type choice and target-choice holes, sibling frontiers exposed together may be filled in either order before advancing to the next d20 frontier. Runtime-backed weapon-attack and partial Command Flee ordering rejections remain explicit invalid fills; save-gated spell, spell-attack, healing, and Command earlier-fill submissions are modeled as earliest-needed-frontier requests when the reducer accepts prefilling rather than rejecting. Table-owned range, cover, sight, area geometry, object target facts, held-object inventory identity, healing-pool range facts, modifier facts, later damage-disposition validation, and stale-subject rejection remain boundary or reducer evidence outside this ordering-error relation. Stat Block scope: the SRD Stat Block entry lists monster Actions, Reactions, Attack Notation, and Damage Notation. The reducer exposes Stat Block action or Multiattack control before constituent attacks, requests target choice before the Stat Block Attack Roll, requests rolled damage dice only after a hit when the chosen Stat Block damage notation uses rolled damage, resolves static-damage branches without a rolled-dice frontier, and requests the start-turn Stat Block Recharge Roll before a recharge-gated action becomes available again. Limited-use availability, Multiattack dispatch resources, Reaction and Legendary Action resource semantics remain covered by BATTLE.STAT_BLOCK.ATTACK_CONTROL; this protocol owner records their reducer-visible hole-frontier order without dispatching on monster authored identity.

The closed fixture covers the named gate and benefit cases: Short Rest and Long Rest start HP gates, 16-hour Long Rest calendar wait rejection, Short Rest and Long Rest duration-proof rejections at the benefit boundary, one-die and two-die sequential Short Rest Hit Point Dice spends, interrupted Short Rest no-benefit, Long Rest HP/Hit Point Dice/max-HP-reduction reset, interrupted Long Rest before/after the one-hour Short Rest benefit threshold, Long Rest physical-exertion threshold rejection, and interruption-at-required-duration rejection. The fixture projects from existing Character Sheet facts into the shared hit-point-recovery semantic core for positive Hit Point healing only; Short Rest timing, Long Rest timing, Hit Point Dice spending, Stable calendar recovery, and positive-Hit-Point healing remain distinct rule facts and runtime owners. The manual Rust dry-run remains documentation-only generator-readiness evidence for the pure healing projection, with no generated Rust source, ABI, or parallel sheet recovery state. Random branch interleavings are not the risk at this sheet boundary.

title: Character Sheet normal and effective Hit Point Maximum derivation from class Hit Dice, level progression, Constitution modifier, deterministic maximum bonuses, and maximum reduction

parityWitnesses.deterministicReplayRationale: DRP-T15 keeps Character Sheet Hit Point Maximum derivation as a deterministic replay. The fixture covers level-1 maximum Hit Die, fixed higher-level gain, multiclass later-level gain, minimum 1 later-level gain, deterministic class-feature maximum bonus, and effective maximum after a maximum reduction. The TS witness derives normal maximum through characterBuildHitPoints from retained class Hit Dice, class level progression, Constitution modifier, and deterministic class-feature facts, then derives effective maximum through Character Sheet maximumHp minus hitPointMaximumReduction; it does not add or compare a second stored maximum state. The input space is scalar arithmetic over existing build and reduction facts with no draft-fill ordering, branch interleaving, or table-choice risk, so focused random MBT would not add coverage.

title: Character Sheet spellbook Ritual invocation projects from existing spellbook Spell Access and Ritual-tagged Spell Definitions

parityWitnesses.deterministicReplayRationale: DRP-T18 keeps Character Sheet spellbook Ritual as a deterministic selected-identity replay. The selected Wizard Ritual Adept fixture covers the accepted spellbook case and the prepared-only rejection case, while concrete Wizard feature, spell, and source identity stay package-boundary evidence. The reusable semantic core owns the identity-free access facts and invocation projection constants: level-1+ Ritual-tagged Spell Definition, spellbook access path, spellbook Ritual Access feature present for that source, no Spell Slot cost, preparation not required, spellbook access, ten extra casting minutes, and reading from the spellbook. The replay also runs deterministic semantic-core branches for non-Ritual, non-leveled, and missing-feature rejection. The runtime projects the invocation from existing CharacterBuild spellbook Spell Access, the installed spellbook Ritual Access feature, and the Surface Spell Definition Ritual tag; it records no separate Ritual list and spends no Spell Slot, so random branch interleavings are not the risk at this projection boundary.

title: Character Sheet projects retained class-feature always-prepared Spell Access without duplicating class prepared-spell state

parityWitnesses.deterministicReplayRationale: DRP-T18 keeps Character Sheet class-feature prepared Spell Access as a deterministic selected-identity replay. The Spell Access fixture covers retained SRD class-feature grants for Life Domain Spells, Circle Spells selected by the current Circle of the Land land choice, Oath of Devotion Spells, Paladin's Smite, Favored Enemy, Draconic Spells, and Fiend Spells; the same selected-identity driver also carries Jack of All Trades unit-gate evidence, but that non-Spell-Access action is outside this obligation's replay decision. The replayed Spell Access facts are projection facts: feature Unit id, selected spellcasting source where the land choice needs one, expected spell membership, spell count, selected land, and acceptance. The runtime projects spell ids directly from retained CharacterBuild class or subclass selections, retained selected-land source facts, and installed Surface class-feature mechanics into sheet Spell Access. It does not store a separate per-class prepared-spell roster, and SRD Always-Prepared spells do not count against a changeable prepared list, so random branch interleavings are not the risk at this projection boundary.

title: Battle reducer spine composition from battle start through act discovery, subject hole/fill resolution, turn advancement, and battle-owned resource/vital projection
reason: This is a thin composition witness for cleanroom reducer architecture, not a replacement for focused rule owners. The MBT trace drives startBattle, discoverBattleActs, and resolveBattleSubject through a Magic Missile spell, End Turn runtime command, and Skeleton Shortsword attack. It asserts closed reducer-spine variants and high-signal projections only: current actor, public hole frontier, action and bonus-action resources, committed spell-slot turn state for this fixture, interrupt-stack depth, reactions as durable creature resources, and caster/target Hit Points. Detailed spell targeting, damage math, attack resolution, turn-boundary effects, and interrupt/resume behavior remain owned by their existing focused QNT rows.

Battle protocol interrupt stack nesting, decline/resume discipline, active Spell Effect resume, and replay-from-root equivalence
reason: This row covers the reducer protocol shape beyond the single Reaction offer: the battle-runtime reaction-window owner projects interrupt stack frames through the existing rule-core ReactionWindowState depth, decline, and advance-continuation semantics, the reaction-resolution owner resumes suspended procedures from the post-Reaction BattleState after active Spell Effects may have changed, and the replay-equivalence owner computes replay-from-root projection by combining the recorded continuation subject/fills with newly supplied suffix fills. The focused witness compares independently resolving recorded subject+fills from the root state against the production replay-continuation frame path over the same root state, recorded continuation, handled trigger, and suffix fill sequence. The SRD anchors the Reaction timing and continuation rule; choosing concrete interrupt stack frames and replay calls is reducer protocol evidence, not a separate RAW ordering interpretation.

title: Battle turn-boundary effect lifecycle ordering across end-turn cleanup, initiative advancement, start-turn spell effects, ongoing-feature expiration, and weapon-hit turn effects
reason: Task PPW-T13 adds a bounded focused MBT witness for the existing reducer order: one source/target fixture carries target start-turn damage/save, target end-turn damage-and-expiry, source until-next-turn expiry, source start-turn ongoing-feature expiry, and target end-turn ongoing-feature expiry across two turn advancements. The witness asserts hole frontier order and state projection only for that fixture; it does not claim exhaustive same-timing ordering. Death Saving Throw ordering is excluded from this covered seam because ASSUMPTIONS.md#A6 records the current fixed death-save-before-start-turn-effects ordering as a RAW-violation owner-decision issue.

title: Battle protocol Concentration break teardown removes the broken Spell Effect before the next command or replacement Concentration effect proceeds
reason: This bounded composition witness covers the reducer seam where damage to a concentrating combatant opens a Concentration Saving Throw continuation, a failed save breaks Concentration and tears down the active Spell Effect before any next command surface is inspected, voluntary Concentration end uses the same teardown owner, and casting another Concentration spell removes the prior Concentration Spell Effect before the replacement effect is active. Incapacitated and death-triggered breaks remain outside this slice; PPW-T14 owns the death path.

title: Battle protocol zero-Hit-Point mid-resolution teardown applies Unconscious, Incapacitated-driven Concentration break, dependent Spell Effect cleanup, and remaining attack sequence resolution against the post-teardown state
reason: This bounded composition witness covers the existing reducer order for same-resolution multi-target spell attack sequencing: Eldritch Blast's first beam damages the concentrating Shield of Faith source, the source succeeds on the damage-triggered Concentration Saving Throw, then dropping to 0 Hit Points applies Unconscious and clears Concentration through the Incapacitated chain. The linked Shield of Faith Armor Class Spell Effect is removed before the second beam attack is evaluated, so an attack total that would miss the shielded target's AC hits the post-teardown target and deals damage. It is fixture-world ordering evidence, not exhaustive multi-target sequencing coverage.
